properties.headline: Flood Warning issued October 28 at 9:03AM EDT until October 29 at 8:00PM EDT by NWS Melbourne FL
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning is extended for the following rivers in
Florida...

St Johns River Near Deland affecting Volusia and Lake Counties.

.Upstream persistent gusty northeast winds and tidal effects on the
St John River are slowing flow. At Deland, the river is forecast to
crest near Minor Flood Stage the next couple days, then begin a slow
decline through Action Stage later in the week.

For the St. Johns River...including Deland...Minor flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Deland.

* WHEN...Until Thursday evening.

* IMPACTS...At 4.0 feet, Docks and piers are completely submerged at
Pier 44 Marina. Many docks are partially submerged at Hontoon
Landing Marina.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 8:30 AM EDT Wednesday the stage was 4.0 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 3.5 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 4.0 feet
the next couple days. It will then fall below flood stage late in
the week.
- Flood stage is 4.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued late tonight at 1215 AM EDT.

properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued October 28 at 3:25PM MDT until October 28 at 6:30PM MDT by NWS Midland/Odessa TX
properties.description:
FFWMAF

The National Weather Service in Midland/Odessa has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Southwestern Eddy County in southeastern New Mexico...

* Until 630 PM MDT.

* At 325 PM MDT, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing
heavy rain across the warned area. The expected rainfall rate is 1
to 1.5 inches in 1 hour. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected to
begin shortly.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban areas,
highways, streets and underpasses as well as other poor
drainage and low-lying areas.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Carlsbad Caverns National Park.
properties.instruction:
In hilly terrain there are hundreds of low water crossings which are
potentially dangerous in heavy rain. Do not attempt to cross flooded
roads. Find an alternate route.

Flooding is occurring or is imminent. It is important to know where
you are relative to streams, rivers, or creeks which can become
killers in heavy rains. Campers and hikers should avoid streams or
creeks.

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued October 28 at 11:45AM MDT by NWS Albuquerque NM
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in New
Mexico...

Rio Chama Below Chamita affecting Rio Arriba County.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Rio Chama below Chamita.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 6.0 feet, Properties in the flood plain along the Rio
Chama and near the junction of the Rio Ojo Caliente will see water
in their yards. Impacts can include bank erosion and damage to
wells and septic tanks.  These impacts will increase in severity at
higher river levels.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 11:00 AM MDT Wednesday the stage was 6.6 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 5.5 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 11:00 AM MDT Wednesday was 6.9 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to remain between 6.4 and 6.7
feet through the next several days.
- Flood stage is 6.0 feet.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 6.7
feet on 07/21/2009.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/abq/EmergencyPrepFlood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov/abq.

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued October 28 at 8:58AM EDT by NWS Melbourne FL
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Astor affecting Volusia and Lake Counties.

.Persistent gusty northeast winds and upstream tidal effects are
slowing river flow on the St Johns River at Astor. River levels are
forecast to begin a slow decline late this week, but remain in
Moderate Flood stage for at least the next couple weeks.

For the St. Johns River...including Deland, Astor...Moderate flooding
is forecast.

* WHAT...Moderate flooding is occurring and is forecast.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Astor.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 4.0 feet, Major flooding occurs with water entering
many structures on canals and along the river. Long duration
flooding will occur, with levels taking weeks to months to return
below flood stage. Water rescues will be necessary. River Road
becomes inaccessible, with 1 to 2 feet water depth in numerous
homes on Wildhog, Possum, Bonnet and Snail roads. Roads along Blue
Creek are inaccessible with major flooding of homes on Otter,
Branch and Chestnut roads. Camp South Moon Road and Juno Trail are
inaccessible.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 8:30 AM EDT Wednesday the stage was 3.7 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 2.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 8:30 AM EDT Wednesday was 3.8 feet.
- Forecast...River levels are forecast to crest around 3.8 feet
this week, then begin a gradual decline late in the week.
- Flood stage is 2.3 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued late tonight at 200 AM EDT.

properties.areaDesc: Silver Bay Harbor to Two Harbors MN; Two Harbors to Duluth MN; Duluth MN to Port Wing WI; Port Wing to Sand Island WI; Lake Superior west of a line from Saxon Harbor WI to Grand Portage MN beyond 5NM
properties.headline: Special Marine Warning issued October 28 at 5:21PM CDT until October 28 at 6:15PM CDT by NWS Duluth MN
properties.description:
SMWDLH

The National Weather Service in Duluth MN has issued a

* Special Marine Warning for...
Duluth MN to Port Wing WI...
Lake Superior west of a line from Saxon Harbor WI to Grand Portage
MN beyond 5NM...
Port Wing to Sand Island WI...
Silver Bay Harbor to Two Harbors MN...
Two Harbors to Duluth MN...

* Until 615 PM CDT.

* At 520 PM CDT, a severe thunderstorm capable of producing
waterspouts was located 8 nm southwest of Superior Harbor, or 12 nm
south of Duluth Lift Bridge Channel, moving northeast at 40 knots.

HAZARD...Waterspouts, wind gusts to 40 knots, and large hail.

SOURCE...Radar.

IMPACT...Waterspouts can easily overturn boats and create locally
hazardous seas. Small craft could be damaged in briefly
higher winds and suddenly higher waves. Large hail could
result in structural damage.

* Locations impacted include...
Superior Entry, Knife River Marina, Castle Danger, Barkers Island,
Duluth Harbor, Duluth Lift Bridge Channel, Twin Points Safe Harbor,
Two Harbors Protected Access Agate Bay, Brule Point, McQuade
Harbor, Superior Harbor, Larsmont, Stoney Point, French River, and
Port Wing Harbor.
properties.instruction:
Move to safe harbor until hazardous weather passes.

Thunderstorms can produce sudden waterspouts. Waterspouts can easily
overturn boats and create locally hazardous seas. Seek safe harbor
immediately.

properties.headline: Severe Thunderstorm Warning issued October 28 at 4:46PM MDT until October 28 at 5:00PM MDT by NWS Albuquerque NM
properties.description:
At 446 PM MDT, a severe thunderstorm was located 6 miles south of
Hondo, or 20 miles east of Ruidoso, moving south at 5 mph.

HAZARD...60 mph wind gusts and small hail.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Expect damage to roofs, siding, and trees.

Locations impacted include...
Mainly rural areas of South Central Lincoln County.
properties.instruction:
Seek shelter inside a well-built structure and stay away from
windows. This storm is capable of producing damaging winds.

Heavy rains from severe thunderstorms can produce sudden and
dangerous flows in arroyos, ditches and over low water crossings. Do
not attempt to drive through areas where water covers the roadway.

NWSheadline: SEVERE THUNDERSTORM WARNING REMAINS IN EFFECT UNTIL 5 PM MDT FOR SOUTH CENTRAL LINCOLN COUNTY

properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued October 28 at 4:13PM MDT until October 28 at 6:45PM MDT by NWS El Paso Tx/Santa Teresa NM
properties.description:
At 413 PM MDT, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing heavy
rain across the warned area. Between 1.5 and 2.5 inches of rain have
fallen. Additional rainfall amounts up to 1 inch are possible in the
warned area. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected to begin shortly.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban areas,
highways, streets and underpasses as well as other poor
drainage and low-lying areas.

Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Mainly rural areas of South Central Otero County.
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Remain alert for flooding even in locations not receiving rain.
Arroyos, streams, and rivers can become raging killer currents in a
matter of minutes, even from distant rainfall.

Please report observed flooding to local emergency services or law
enforcement and request they pass this information to the National
Weather Service when you can do so safely.

NWSheadline: FLASH FLOOD WARNING REMAINS IN EFFECT UNTIL 645 PM MDT THIS EVENING FOR SOUTH CENTRAL OTERO COUNTY
